s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with seizures, hemiparesis, and developmental delays
salient_findings: Upper motor neuron pattern of weakness
Focal abnormal brain activity on EEG
key_facts: Age of seizure onset: 3 months
Seizures have increased in frequency despite antiepileptic therapy
Delayed motor and cognitive milestones
Gradual behavioral changes, including disturbed sleep and irritability
No family history of neurological disorders
No reported perinatal complications or trauma
Normal routine laboratory studies, including metabolic and infectious panels
EEG shows focal abnormal brain activity
MRI demonstrates cerebral hemisphere atrophy and ex vacuo dilatation of the lateral ventricle
Ipsilateral calvarial thickening and compensatory hyperpneumatization of the sphenoid bone and bilateral mastoid air cells
Cystic encephalomalacia and gliosis in the right fronto-parieto-temporal region

shortlist.label: Rasmussen's encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Focal seizures, hemiparesis, and progressive neurological decline

shortlist.label: Hemimegalencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Cerebral hemisphere atrophy and ex vacuo dilatation of the lateral ventricle

shortlist.label: Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Cerebral hemiatrophy and compensatory hyperpneumatization of the sphenoid bone and bilateral mastoid air cells

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Seizures, hemiparesis, and possible calvarial thickening

shortlist.label: Porencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic encephalomalacia and gliosis in the right fronto-parieto-temporal region

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of seizures, left-sided weakness, developmental delays, and marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres with atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere and ex vacuo dilatation of the right lateral ventricle, along with ipsilateral calvarial thickening, is most consistent with Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome, which is characterized by cerebral hemiatrophy, often with a history of seizures and contralateral hemiparesis.

rejected.label: Rasmussen's encephalitis
rejected.why: Rasmussen's encephalitis typically presents with more rapid progression of symptoms, including seizures and hemiparesis, and often involves more widespread inflammation and atrophy, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Hemimegalencephaly
rejected.why: Hemimegalencephaly is characterized by overgrowth of one cerebral hemisphere, which is not consistent with the atrophy described in this patient.

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: Sturge-Weber syndrome typically involves a port-wine stain and leptomeningeal angiomatosis, which are not mentioned in this case.

rejected.label: Porencephaly
rejected.why: Porencephaly typically involves a cystic cavity within the brain, often resulting from perinatal injury or infection, which is not the primary finding in this case, although cystic encephalomalacia is present, it is not the dominant feature.
